title: The Cat and the Birds
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Cat heard that the Birds in an aviary were ailing. So he got himself up as a doctor, and, taking with him a set of the instruments proper to his profession, presented himself at the door, and inquired after the health of the Birds. "We shall do very well," they replied, without letting him in, "when we've seen the last of you."
A villain may disguise himself, but he will not deceive the wise.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Cat hear about the Birds in the aviary?
options: That they were about to be sold
That they had escaped their cage
That they were ailing
That they were being fed too much

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does the Cat disguise himself?
options: As a doctor
As a birdkeeper
As a merchant selling seed
As another bird

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Cat bring with him to seem convincing?
options: A basket of medicine and herbs
A letter of introduction
A cage to carry the sick birds
A set of instruments proper to his profession

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Cat do once he reaches the door?
options: He knocks loudly and demands to be let in
He inquires after the health of the Birds
He begins treating the Birds through the bars
He leaves a note and departs at once

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what do the Birds say they need to "do very well"?
options: To be given proper medicine
To be moved to a larger aviary
To see the last of the Cat
To have the doctor return tomorrow

questions.prompt: According to the passage, do the Birds let the Cat inside?
options: No, they answer without letting him in
Yes, they open the door at once
Yes, but only after questioning him first
No, because they had already flown away

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Cat disguise himself as a doctor in the first place?
options: He genuinely wants to help cure the Birds' illness
He is being paid by the aviary's owner to check on them
He wants to learn more about medicine from the Birds
He hopes the disguise will let him get close enough to harm the Birds

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Birds' reply reveal about whether the disguise worked?
options: They were fully convinced he was a real doctor
They saw through it and knew the Cat was still a danger to them
They were unsure but let him in out of caution
They believed him but were too weak to respond

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "ailing" mean in "the Birds in an aviary were ailing"?
options: Singing loudly
Multiplying quickly
Sick or unwell
Fighting each other

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable, given its closing line?
options: A disguise cannot fool those who already know your true nature
Doctors should never visit birds without an invitation
Birds are always too weak to protect themselves from cats
It is wise to let strangers in no matter their appearance

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where do the Birds that the Cat visits live?
options: In a barn loft
In a garden hedge
In a hollow tree
In an aviary

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Cat ask about when he arrives?
options: The price of the aviary
The health of the Birds
The number of Birds inside
The owner of the aviary

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what do the Birds say will happen once they've "seen the last" of the Cat?
options: They shall call for a real doctor
They shall finally recover their strength
They shall do very well
They shall be moved somewhere safer

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why do the instruments the Cat carries matter to his plan?
options: They are meant to make his disguise as a doctor look convincing
They are the tools he actually plans to use to cure the Birds
They are gifts he intends to give to the Birds
They belong to a real doctor he is imitating exactly

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what makes the Birds' brief reply an effective way to refuse the Cat?
options: It invites him in while warning him to behave
It admits they are too sick to argue with him
It asks him to come back with real medicine instead
It politely but firmly turns him away without ever opening the door

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does it mean that the Cat "got himself up" as a doctor?
options: He argued loudly that he was one
He dressed and equipped himself to look like one
He studied for years to become one
He was hired officially to act as one

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Cat successfully cures the Birds of their illness
A Cat is invited in and shares a meal with the Birds
A Cat disguises himself as a doctor, but the Birds refuse to let him in
A Cat gives up his disguise before reaching the aviary
